newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler sees management revamp decision by yr-end.
newsitem.headline: Daimler sees management revamp decision by yr-end.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG chairman Juergen Schrempp said the company hopes to make a decision on a management restructuring by the end of the year.
Interviewed on CNN television, Schrempp said: "We will be talking for a number of weeks. Toward the end of the year we will announce which way we are going."
Schrempp said the group is considering how to make decision-making faster and quality better.
"We are now looking at various (management) models."
Schrempp was speaking on CNN's Moneyline programme, a recorded version of which was aired on Friday morning in Europe.
News magazine Der Spiegel reported in this week's editions that Schrempp had put forward various radical options for a revamp at an internal management meeting last week.
One of the ideas envisaged removing the management board level at Daimler's large subsidiaries, Spiegel reported.
Another idea involved transforming Daimler into a pure financial holding company and strengthening the power of subsidiaries, the report said.
But Spiegel added that any decision on a management reorganisation would only be reached by consensus. The ideas represented extreme positions and hence could barely be realised, it said.

Any complete removal of the subsidiaries' management power would be blocked by Helmut Werner, management board chairman of Daimler's flagship car and truckmaking unit Mercedes-Benz AG, the report said.
And a transfer of power to subsidiaries would not be in Schrempp's interest, it added.
